Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary + attachments below.

What we're sending (attached):
- no-learning-ops-checklist.pdf — step-by-step ops and attestations we can provide; shows hooks at request routing, runtime flags, and data flow diagrams.
- subprocessors-2027-09.csv — current subprocessor inventory with geographic residency and function.

Answers to your bullets:
1) No-adaptive-training: Redwood supports a per-customer flag that disables model-improvement paths at the serving runtime. When enabled, requests are served from read-only checkpoints and no tokens are included in downstream model training pipelines. The checklist includes: runtime flag locations, compilation/kernels safe paths, and automated audits that run weekly. We can provide a signed attestation and an operational screenshot of the flag state.

2) Subprocessors: attached CSV contains names and details. Any subprocessor that performs storage or long-term logging for Orchard Health's account can be restricted to our onshore residency pool; we can map each subprocessor to the account-level residency constraint.

3) Export lanes: we support two export lanes for production pilots — SFTP push (preferred for bulk exports) and a secured REST export API (for programmatic pull). See export-lane-specs.md for formats (JSONL with metadata headers), manifest files, and retention/deletion markers. Exports are signed and checksummed.

4) Deletion and ephemeral options: we support ephemeral KV caches (TTL-based), prompt redaction, and an API-triggered deletion job that returns a job id + proof-of-deletion manifest. The checklist shows how deletion is validated and logged.

On ownership and amendment: Redwood is willing to accept explicit no-adaptive-training language and a prompt/response ownership clause that keeps derivative rights with Orchard Health for content you send and receive. We'll propose precise language in the DPA addendum (I attached a draft redlines file).

Next steps:
- Kimberly, David: can you review the export-lane-specs and confirm the SFTP endpoint / onshore KMS approach?
- Marta: I'll compile the attestation and SOC2 extract (redacted) and upload to the Drive link by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Sofia
Head of Solutions — East
Redwood Inference

Marta — adding technical detail you can share with engineering and legal. Short version up top, more detail below.

Short answers:
- Prompts/responses you send to Redwood are mapped to your tenant and are exportable on request; Orchard retains IP for prompt and output artifacts.
- Telemetry we retain for runtime health (latency histograms, sampling of token-level traces) can be scoped and sampled; by default we retain minimal telemetry for 30 days but can reduce sampling to meet your GDPR/contract needs.
- No-adaptive-training is implemented via an account-level runtime toggle that excludes all ingestion into model-improvement pipelines and excludes request logs from any offline training stores.

Technical notes (for your engineers/legal):
- Runtime: requests traverse ingress -> routing -> serving runtime. The 'no-learn' flag is evaluated at routing and appended to the request envelope. Serving nodes open model checkpoints in read-only mode. Any KV writes for session-state are kept ephemeral if configured; persistent logs to S3-compatible stores are gated behind the 'persist_logs' config per-tenant.
- Export lanes: our SFTP exporter writes compressed JSONL manifests with a header line including tenant_id, sequence range, and a SHA256 checksum. The REST export returns a signed URL (short-lived) and a manifest id. Both provide a deletion marker when the dataset is removed.
- Proof of deletion: deletion jobs generate a signed manifest listing file ids and a deletion timestamp; we can provide a hash of deleted records for your audit team. For higher assurance, we offer onshore escrow where a separate process verifies bucket lifecycle deletion.
- Subprocessors & KMS: we can route key operations to an onshore KMS namespace (customer key alias) and restrict storage subprocessors used for persistent exports to certified onshore providers.

Attachment: export-lane-specs.md (contains sample SFTP manifest, example JSONL record, and manifest verification steps).

I'll also prepare a short technical attestation (one page) describing the no-learn enforcement points and an ops contact for the pilot.

Regards,
David Kim
Principal Privacy Engineer
Redwood Inference

(attachment: export-lane-specs.md)
